APL synapses project · step-by-step reports · Report 01 · 2026-10-23

Connectome data: APL synapse tables and per-cell counts

QuestionWhere do the APL synapse tables come from, what does one row mean, how are synapses counted, and how many synapses does APL make with each kind of partner in each part of the mushroom body?
Inputs
  • Public synapse tables of four adult fly connectomes (downloaded 2026-10-07; sources in Table 2)
Outputs
  • <dataset>_APL_MB_synapses.csv.gz: one row per APL synapse in the mushroom body (four datasets)
  • KC_weights_APL_PN_per_KC.csv: per Kenyon cell, its PN input and its synapses with APL (calyx and whole mushroom body)
  • PN_calyx_weights_APL_vs_KC.csv, PN_MB_weights_APL_vs_KC.csv: per projection neuron, its synapses onto KCs and with APL
  • summary_counts_by_compartment_and_partner_class.csv, the scatter plots scatter*.png
Scripts
  • scripts/hemibrain.py, malecns.py, malecns2.py, fafb_princeton.py, banc_extract.py (download and filter)
  • scripts/prep.py, run.py, export.py (regions, compartments, claws, boutons, export)
  • scripts/scatter.py, mb_plots.py, pnmb_*.py (per-cell counts and scatter plots)
  • scripts/reports/r01_connectome_tables.py (this report)

Every later step starts from the tables described here. Reports 02 and 03 add structure to them (claws, boutons, odor responses); Reports 04 to 11 use the hemibrain and male CNS parts of them to build and test a model. This report uses the tables with the official regions of interest (ROIs) only. Report 02 describes the second version, which adds synapses that lie just outside the official ROIs.

1The four connectomes and how each synapse is counted

A connectome is a map of every neuron and synapse in a piece of nervous tissue, traced from electron microscopy. A chemical synapse is seen as one presynaptic release site (the T-bar) facing one or more postsynaptic densities (PSDs) on other neurons. All tables here count T-bar → PSD pairs: one T-bar facing three PSDs on three cells counts once for each cell, so the weight wijw_{ij}wij​ is the number of PSDs on jjj that face T-bars of iii. This is the convention of neuPrint (hemibrain, male CNS) and FlyWire.

wij(R)  =  #{(t,s) : t is a T-bar of i, s is a PSD of j facing t, s∈R}(1)w_{ij}(\mathcal{R}) \;=\; \#\{(t, s)\ :\ t \text{ is a T-bar of } i,\ s \text{ is a PSD of } j \text{ facing } t,\ s \in \mathcal{R}\} \tag{1}wij​(R)=#{(t,s) : t is a T-bar of i, s is a PSD of j facing t, s∈R}(1)
A synapse belongs to region R\mathcal{R}R by the position of its postsynaptic site (hemibrain, male CNS) or by the dataset's own neuropil label (FlyWire, BANC).

The APL neuron (anterior paired lateral) is one large GABAergic neuron per brain hemisphere. It covers the whole mushroom body, receives input from the Kenyon cells and inhibits them back. Every APL synapse inside a mushroom body ROI was kept, in both directions and with every partner.

Why BANC counts are low

BANC has 3–5 times fewer APL synapses than the other datasets (median KC↔APL synapses per KC in the calyx: 2 vs 10 in hemibrain). This follows from its synapse detector and the size ≥ 5 filter, and it is why BANC numbers are treated as rough throughout.

Two FlyWire versions

The FlyWire rows in the main table keep only neuron pairs with ≥5 synapses (Codex default). The per-KC and per-PN counts (Section 5) instead use every Princeton synapse between proofread neurons, without that threshold, because a KC often makes fewer than 5 synapses with APL in the calyx. So FlyWire per-cell counts are larger than counts from the main table.

2What one row of the table is

Each row is one T-bar → PSD pair where APL is on one side. The columns that the later steps use:

Table 3. Main columns of <dataset>_APL_MB_synapses.csv.gz. The README lists every column.
ColumnMeaning
directionAPL_output (APL presynaptic): APL → partner. APL_input (APL postsynaptic): partner → APL.
apl_id, apl_sideWhich APL. Each mushroom body has its own APL, so "APL side" = which mushroom body.
partner_id, partner_type, partner_classThe other neuron, its cell type and its broad class (blank = untyped fragment)
pre_*_nm, post_*_nmPositions of the T-bar and the PSD, in nanometres, in the dataset's own coordinate space
partner_side_*_nmThe partner's own site (the PSD when APL is presynaptic, the T-bar when APL is postsynaptic); used to place a synapse on a claw or bouton
roi_official, mb_regionThe dataset's own ROI label, and the mushroom body region: CA, PED, or a lobe
mb_compartment, mb_compartment_sourceThe finest compartment label (α1 … γ5 in the lobes) and whether it is official or derived (Section 4)
claw_id, bouton_id (and nearest_*, *_dist_nm)The KC claw or PN bouton the synapse sits on, if any (Report 02)

3Regions of the mushroom body and how many APL synapses each has

The mushroom body has three parts. The calyx (CA) is where projection neurons (PNs) from the antennal lobe pass odor information to the dendritic claws of the Kenyon cells (KCs). The peduncle (PED) is the bundle of KC axons leaving the calyx. The lobes are where KC axons end and talk to output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs). Hemibrain and male CNS split the lobes into α, α′, β, β′ and γ lobes; FlyWire and BANC only into a vertical lobe (VL: α + α′) and a medial lobe (ML: β + β′ + γ).

In every dataset APL makes more synapses than it receives in the calyx (APL output share of calyx APL synapses: FlyWire 783 55%, Hemibrain v1.2 60%, Male CNS v1.0 60%, BANC 888 59%). In the lobes the two directions are closer to equal.

3.1Who APL talks to

Kenyon cells are by far APL's main partner everywhere. In the calyx, PNs are the second partner (9–12% of APL synapses there): APL inhibits the PN boutons as well as the KC claws, which Reports 04 and 05 use.

4Lobe compartments

Each lobe is divided into compartments (α1–3, α′1–3, β1–2, β′1–2, γ1–5), each defined by which DAN and MBON types innervate it. Only the male CNS publishes compartment volumes (malecns-subcompartments-v3); there the official label is used. For the other datasets the compartment of a lobe synapse is derived from the dopaminergic neurons around it:

  1. In male CNS, measure for each DAN family (e.g. PAM12, PPL101) what fraction of its T-bars falls in each compartment: P(c∣ϕ)P(c\mid\phi)P(c∣ϕ) for compartment ccc and family ϕ\phiϕ.
  2. For a synapse sss in a lobe, take the kNN=15k_{\mathrm{NN}}=15kNN​=15 nearest DAN T-bars inside the same lobe ROI.
  3. Each of them votes with its family's distribution. The compartment with the largest summed vote wins (Equation 2); compartment_vote_share is that vote divided by the total, a confidence between 0 and 1.
  4. A synapse whose nearest DAN T-bar is more than 8 µm away gets no compartment.
c^(s)  =  arg⁡max⁡c ∈ lobe(s)∑d ∈ kNN(s)P(c∣ϕ(d))(2)\hat c(s) \;=\; \arg\max_{c\,\in\,\mathrm{lobe}(s)} \sum_{d\,\in\,\mathrm{kNN}(s)} P\big(c \mid \phi(d)\big) \tag{2}c^(s)=argc∈lobe(s)max​d∈kNN(s)∑​P(c∣ϕ(d))(2)
c^(s)\hat c(s)c^(s): derived compartment of synapse sss; kNN(s)\mathrm{kNN}(s)kNN(s): its 15 nearest DAN T-bars in the same lobe; ϕ(d)\phi(d)ϕ(d): the family of DAN T-bar ddd.

Check against the official volumes. Applied to the male CNS itself, the derived label matches the official one for 96.9% of 311,252 lobe synapses when the lobe is known (the hemibrain situation). The weakest compartment is γ3 (78%). With only the coarse VL/ML lobes (FlyWire, BANC) the agreement was 88%, mainly because α′2 is then called α2. For the per-KC lobe plots a refined vote (DAN T-bars restricted to the KC's own lobe) reaches 97.9%.

Not used by the model

Compartments matter only for the lobe scatter plots (scatter4–scatter7). The model in Reports 05–11 uses calyx synapses only.

6Caveats

  • Detection differs between datasets. Each connectome has its own synapse detector and thresholds, so absolute counts are not comparable across datasets; ratios and ranks within a dataset are safer. The model (Reports 05–11) works with ratios and ranks.
  • Male CNS calyx ROI. The official CA(L)/CA(R) ROIs leave out the posterior part of each calyx: 18% (left) and 9% (right) of PN↔APL and 33% / 14% of KC↔APL calyx synapses fall outside them. The second version adds them back (Report 02).
  • Untyped partners. Partners without a type are 9% of hemibrain rows, 10% of male CNS rows and 39% of BANC rows.
  • Hemibrain types. partner_type is the official neuPrint v1.2 type. A compiled table had labelled about 200 α′β′ KCs as γ; that was corrected on 2026-10-10.
  • Summary table. summary_counts_by_compartment_and_partner_class.csv was made from an earlier hemibrain table; 5 hemibrain γ3–γ5 rows differ by 1–4 synapses from the main table.
